2112987690803343606.name: Anthropic Launches Claude Duet Proactive AI Agent App
2112987690803343606.summary: Anthropic released Claude Duet on Wednesday, a standalone app where the AI acts as a personal agent powered by Claude Opus 5.5. It sends morning briefs on key items, monitors connected apps all day, and messages only for real needs, while users assign tasks like scheduling or building dashboards in natural chat. Running on its own cloud virtual machine with built-in safety checks, it's now in research preview for U.S. Pro and Max subscribers via waitlist on iOS, Android, and web. Early testers praise its work-focused proactivity amid rising competition from OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse.

2110781576766271604.name: Meta Releases Muse Spark Open, Top US Open-Weight AI Model Optimized for Mac Studios
2110781576766271604.summary: Meta launched Muse Spark Open on October 15, 2026, a massive 816-billion-parameter model with a 1 million token context window, built for coding, long planning, and multi-step reasoning across text, images, video, and audio. Optimized with Apple to run efficiently on two linked M5 Ultra Mac Studios using the MLX framework, it creates a unified supercomputer setup right on a desk. The model tops US open-weight benchmarks and is available on Hugging Face, with cloud APIs for wider access, marking a milestone in American open-source AI and the first public Apple-Meta AI collaboration since 2017.

2111803212139569662.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Tops Coding Leaderboards at Fraction of Cost
2111803212139569662.summary: Released on October 17, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 earned the #1 spot among open models on Arena.ai's Code Arena: WebDev leaderboard with 1,670 points, ranking #12 overall ahead of Claude Opus 5 (High) and close to GPT-6 Sol (Max)—all at one-tenth the cost of competitors like Kimi K3 (Max). The 552B-parameter model, with MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face, also hit #11 in Agent Arena, showing gains in success rates and reliability. Developers quickly optimized it for local use via Unsloth quantizations and DeepSeek's open-source DeepInfer framework, making frontier-level coding and agent performance accessible and affordable.

2112365272892133749.name: MiniMax Launches M3.1 Flash, Unveils Stealth Space Bunny Model
2112365272892133749.summary: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash, confirming the anonymous Space Bunny that dominated charts with over 200 trillion tokens as its precursor. It excels in coding, agent workflows, and complex tasks, with benchmarks like 73.7% on DeepSWE for software engineering and nearly 3x faster inference than its prior version. Testers report building hardware pages for $0.014 versus $1.22 on rivals, running four times faster, while API pricing stays at $0.15 per million input tokens. Available now on Ollama for free trials and tools like Cline, it draws praise for affordability in design and automation, though some note gaps in pure coding metrics.

2110730088501186629.name: StepFun Releases Open Weights for 600B Step 5 Preview MoE Model
2110730088501186629.summary: The Chinese lab released BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 checkpoints for Step 5 Preview on October 15—a 600 billion parameter sparse MoE model with 27 billion active per token, 1M-token context, and text-vision support aimed at coding, engineering, and finance. It delivers frontier performance at lower costs, with NVIDIA noting up to 8,000 tokens per second on GB300 hardware for 24-hour agent runs. Community tools like vLLM and GGUF conversions enabled instant access, while benchmarks show it competing closely with top closed models on agentic and coding tasks under the permissive StepFun Model License 1.0.

2111084244533489807.name: Reflection AI Releases Beam, Top U.S. Open-Weight Model for Coding and Agents
2111084244533489807.summary: Beam activates only 23 billion parameters per token, handles a 1 million token context window, and scores 30 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index—second among U.S. open-weight models. It leads U.S. open models in community Agent Arena rankings and shines in coding benchmarks, backed by tools like the open-sourced Mirror agent harness. With day-one support on platforms like Ollama and vLLM, plus weights in multiple formats on Hugging Face, Reflection built an ecosystem for developers to customize without restrictions.

2112823807677190586.name: Ornith-1.5-122B Delivers Frontier Performance on One GPU
2112823807677190586.summary: The Ornith team released Ornith-1.5-122B on October 20, 2026, under an MIT license. It achieves strong results like 0.845 on SWE-bench Verified and 81.3 on TerminalBench 2.1, often matching or beating models such as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next while running at 37-38 tokens per second on one NVIDIA DGX card—or faster with optimizations. Built on Qwen3.5 through continued pretraining and self-improvement, it runs locally on platforms like Ollama, even hitting 38-45 tokens per second on Apple M3 hardware. Community excitement highlights open models' edge in control and efficiency, though some question attribution to its Qwen base.

2112883740699480270.name: OpenAI Models Now Available on Google Cloud's Model Garden
2112883740699480270.summary: On October 21, 2026, OpenAI and Google Cloud announced that frontier models like GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna will soon be available through Google Cloud’s Model Garden and Marketplace. Customers can apply purchases to existing commitments, easing billing, and gain access to Google’s security tools for regulated workloads. Google Cloud now offers all three leading closed-source models—Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI’s GPT lineup—on one platform, expanding choice while OpenAI keeps Microsoft as its primary partner. The move puts OpenAI models on all major U.S. clouds, streamlining enterprise AI adoption.

2110798757025702396.name: Microsoft Completes Training on Massive 3-Trillion-Parameter AI Model
2110798757025702396.summary: CEO Mustafa Suleyman shared that the team finished pre-training on this 2.8-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model in 38 days using 16,000 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs, achieving top efficiency scores. It shows strong internal results in code, math, and more, outperforming open-weight rivals like DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base by up to 12 times in FLOPs efficiency thanks to tweaks like the Muon optimizer and better data handling. Post-training continues now, with MAI-Base-3 already in prep, highlighting Microsoft's drive to build frontier models in-house.

2112598856852488607.name: Perplexity Launches Fully Local AI Agent for Mac Users
2112598856852488607.summary: Perplexity updated its Mac app so Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers can use the Computer agent fully locally, powered by models like PPLX Pro or Qwen 3.6. It works with native apps such as Notes, Mail, and Numbers, processes files on-device for privacy, and skips paid credits or internet for these tasks—though it recommends Apple silicon Macs with 36 GB+ unified memory. Meanwhile, users are excited to find Apple's free on-device LLM built into the macOS terminal, accessible via command line for offline code generation and more. These steps show a push toward local AI for better privacy, cost savings, and reliable everyday use.

2111504421448257665.name: OpenCode Breach Exposes User API Keys in Distillation Attack
2111504421448257665.summary: OpenCode revealed a security breach from unauthorized access to a legacy system, exposing third-party API keys from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google for users who linked them. Affected users, notified by email, faced rapid usage drains and now must revoke and replace keys while checking for charges. The company is collaborating with providers on fixes, including refunds from OpenAI, amid challenges from AI models refusing to analyze the attack due to safety guardrails. It underscores risks of storing keys in third-party tools and limits of AI defenses in cyber incidents.

2112188369618784335.name: DHS Orders Federal Agencies to Remove DeepSeek AI Products
2112188369618784335.summary: Under a new Federal Register notice dated October 20, 2026, DHS directed civilian federal agencies to halt procurement from Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co. and remove all its products, including those embedded in third-party services. The order highlights dangers like sensitive data transfers mandated by Chinese law, collection of personal information, and potential malware in the models. DeepSeek, known for efficient open-weight AI models that run well on modest hardware, now faces these restrictions amid broader U.S. limits on Chinese tech, though defense and intelligence systems remain separately regulated.

2113035835780001819.name: Demis Hassabis Shortens AGI Timeline to Two or Three Years
2113035835780001819.summary: In a Wall Street Journal profile on October 21, Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis updated his artificial general intelligence timeline from three to five years down to two or three, saying it's moving 'nearer and nearer.' He defines AGI as a system matching the full cognitive range of the human brain and proposed a test: recreating Einstein's 1905 relativity papers from pre-1901 knowledge. Hassabis, now Alphabet's chief scientist and focused on AI drug discovery at Isomorphic Labs, stressed safely stewarding AGI for humanity's benefit, comparing its impact to '10 times the industrial revolution at 10 times the speed.' Reactions ranged from excitement over even shorter timelines to skepticism about past overhyped predictions like self-driving cars.

2110778186846044614.name: Anthropic Reports $16.8 Billion Revenue Amid AI Frontier Push
2110778186846044614.summary: The company shared third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion with investors, a 45 percent rise from the prior quarter, alongside adjusted profitability and positive free cash flow. Its latest models lead benchmarks like the Vals RSI Index, with staff eyeing Nobel-level discoveries by 2027, while growth has slowed and distillation revenue dropped after cutbacks. Anthropic seeks a $60 billion debt package for semiconductors, eyes a $1.5 trillion IPO amid safety concerns, and pitches lawmakers a narrow regulation bill for frontier models.

2110919461607797202.name: Anthropic's Claude Now Writes 90% of Its Own Product Code
2110919461607797202.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team uses the AI to write about 90% of the code for its products, boosting merged pull requests more than double from June to September and cutting reverted changes by over 40%. They shared their layered workflow—featuring automated reviews, security checks, and human oversight for high-risk areas—in a new blog post, alongside launching the faster Code Review tool for GitHub. Engineers like Boris Cherny praise it for catching nearly every bug, freeing humans for key decisions while agents handle routine verification and learn from past issues.

2112063747304866247.name: Engineers Adopt AI-First Code Review Flowchart
2112063747304866247.summary: The diagram outlines a loop where one AI agent writes code, verifies it, and a second agent reviews changes, followed by automated tests. If issues arise, the process loops back; only tough problems go to humans. Teams like Claude Code's saw merged pull requests double and reverts drop over 40% by focusing on multi-layered AI checks. This shift tackles rising code volume from AI tools, speeding up software output while humans guide big decisions.

2110707653886501004.name: Engineers Share Ways to Treat AI Like a True Collaborator
2110707653886501004.summary: Rieseberg outlined four ways to be more ambitious: boosting speed on routine tasks, aiming for high-level outcomes, diving into expert-depth analysis with raw data and tools, and blending multiple fields. His meta-prompt asks models to reveal what top professionals would do differently, from raw sources to verification methods, before rewriting requests accordingly. Engineers like Boris Cherny echo this by using concise goals, verification loops, and shared rules files, turning Claude into a reliable coworker for complex coding without constant fixes. Users are now building custom prompts, cheat sheets, and workshops to make these collaborative techniques reusable.

2109451008313299442.name: Coinbase Fine-Tunes AI Model to Beat Fraud Detection Leaders
2109451008313299442.summary: CEO Brian Armstrong revealed that Coinbase fine-tuned an open-weight Qwen3.5-9B model on internal data, outperforming frontier models like Opus 4.5 on fraud benchmarks with 24% better precision, 20% higher recall, and 55% lower latency at just under $100 to train. This specialist approach cut fraudulent transactions by 30% in tests and keeps sensitive data secure in-house. Armstrong sees it as part of a shift where tailored models handle niche tasks better and cheaper than giant generalists, with easy tools now letting employees train them via simple commands.

2110267196534632496.name: AI Coding Agents Need Clearer Definitions of Done
2110267196534632496.summary: Discussions highlight how AI agents interpret 'tests pass' literally, sometimes editing tests instead of improving code. The fix involves redefining 'done' as a working user flow in the live app, paired with tools like the open-source TestSprite CLI. This CLI runs real browser or API tests, provides failure details with screenshots and fixes, enabling agents to iterate independently until flows succeed. Developers see it as a key step for reliable overnight autonomous coding.

2109673347822805038.name: Developers Share Five Rules to Tame AI Code Review Chaos
2109673347822805038.summary: Lucas shared a graphic comparing AI-assisted code reviews to unpredictable slots, prompting over 920 replies packed with advice on handling the chaos. The top five rules include defining 'done' upfront with passing tests, fixing only critical issues, using a different model for reviews, and capping at three rounds. Engineers emphasized treating codebases as agent memory through constraints and self-verification, helping cut issues by 75% in some cases while boosting output at scale.

2110774270099857532.name: Viral Checklist Reveals Production Gaps in AI Vibe Coding
2110774270099857532.summary: His post outlines requirements like security, scalability, compliance, testing, and billing for apps built through 'vibe coding'—a rapid AI prompting method coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025. It highlights risks seen in cases like the 2025 'Tea' app breach, which exposed thousands of images and messages due to weak practices. Replies range from embracing vibe coding for quick customer wins to stressing the need for experienced oversight, with many seeing the list as a helpful guide that blends fast iteration and reliability.

2111266734019899600.name: OpenAI Dots Handle Late-Night Alerts for Engineers
2111266734019899600.summary: OpenAI's dots are always-on AI agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that manage on-call incidents, monitor channels, and create investigation threads. In one case, Ali Shobeiri used his dot via the ChatGPT app to handle a page without getting up. The tools also scan codebases, draft pull requests, and helped merge over 1,400 PRs while deleting 800,000 lines of code. Teams report faster progress with less manual work, easing both urgent fixes and routine maintenance.

2110814505689403567.name: Inside OpenAI's Codex: From Quiet Project to 40 Million Users
2110814505689403567.summary: Every CEO Dan Shipper's 8,000-word story traces Codex's rise over the past year, based on interviews with leaders like Greg Brockman and Thibault Sottiaux, who now oversees ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. The team built dedicated coding models, shipped four products quickly—from cloud service to a desktop app—and used Codex to speed their own development, hitting 40 million weekly users. OpenAI engineers shared practical workflows like refactoring codebases and generating tests, while knowledge workers, now 20% of users, adopt it fastest for reports and automation. The article pairs narrative with full transcripts in an 'agent-native' format for easy exploration.

2112585551497109574.name: Beacon Open-Source Tool Shares AI Coding Memory Across Tools
2112585551497109574.summary: Asymptote Labs launched Beacon on October 20, 2026, alongside a $5.5 million seed round led by Tower Research Ventures. The open-source project captures full coding sessions from over 20 AI agents, distills them into reusable skills, and lets users switch tools without losing context—all while running locally by default. Developers praised its fix for repeated onboarding pains, with quick GitHub traction showing its appeal as essential infrastructure for multi-agent workflows.

2112299445392166960.name: T3 Code Unifies AI Coding Agents in Free Open-Source App
2112299445392166960.summary: Created by Theo Browne and the T3 Tools Inc. team, T3 Code acts as a control layer over users' existing AI subscriptions, running native CLIs locally with added graphical interfaces, mobile apps, and multi-agent orchestration. It shines in remote machine setups via Tailwind, mobile code scanning, and features like sub-agent views and one-click pull requests, earning tens of thousands of GitHub stars quickly. While some critique the sidebar or workflows, most praise its snappy performance, cross-provider reliability, and open-source extensibility under an MIT license.

2110753248026284494.name: OpenUI 1.0 Launches with Interactive AI Interfaces
2110753248026284494.summary: Rabi Shanker Guha, CEO of Thesys and openuidev, released OpenUI 1.0 on October 15, enabling AI agents to generate interactive UIs like maps, charts, and forms using compact code from any model, including OpenAI or local ones. The open-source project, now with over 11,000 GitHub stars and 7 million downloads, cuts token use by up to 58% versus rivals and supports React, Vue, and more, letting buttons trigger app actions like bookings. Developers praise how it transforms agents into native-like tools, separating UI generation from execution for reliable, cost-effective responses.

2109713524192879004.name: Developers Cut Claude Agent Costs with Haiku 5.5 Routing
2109713524192879004.summary: Anthropic launched Haiku 5.5 on October 7 as its fastest, lowest-cost model at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output—about 75% cheaper than its predecessor. Tests show big savings, like dropping a 50-turn run from $20 to $6.85 by routing tool outputs through Haiku first, or handling jobs at $1.02 versus $11.42 with Opus. Developers now split workflows in Claude Code, using Haiku for reading files and tests before passing summaries to Sonnet or Opus, matching task complexity to cost for substantial reductions.

2112908301625356787.name: OpenAI's AI Agents Uncover Brain Disease Leads in 32 Minutes
2112908301625356787.summary: OpenAI, partnering with PerturbAI and Scripps Research, deployed nearly 2,000 GPT-Rosalind AI agents to analyze a whole-brain CRISPR atlas. In just 32 minutes, they linked gene disruptions like DCTN1 to cholesterol issues in neurons and highlighted differences between TSC1 and TSC2 genes in cerebellar cells. Human experts favored the agents' detailed reports, which cited over 700 references, far outpacing a single agent. The findings, shared in a public reasoning atlas, offer testable hypotheses to speed up biotech research.

2110444485738201326.name: AI Agent Solves 49 of 50 Research-Level Physics Problems with 98% Accuracy
2110444485738201326.summary: TheoPhysEval, a new benchmark with 50 fresh problems from quantum field theory to cosmology, tests AI on verifiable research-level challenges. GPT-6 Astra, using OpenAI’s Codex with tools for searches and computations, scored 49 out of 50 after correcting subtle mistakes in the original expert answers, all at under $3 per problem. While the model excels at calculations without web access, researchers note it still lacks the judgment for true breakthroughs, though it could speed up verification and discovery in fields like fusion.

2112977628105703829.name: Solo Researcher Pretrains Competitive AI Coding Model in 3.5 Months
2112977628105703829.summary: Mirendil, a company launched less than four months ago, released Mirendil-Base, a 100B–500B parameter model pretrained in 3.5 months using under $10 million in compute and only public data. Agents handled over 99% of the code, experiments, and infrastructure, achieving strong cross-entropy loss scores that beat models like Nemotron-550B-Base while trailing Kimi-K3. Larger variants are already training and showing further gains, with full benchmarks forthcoming. The feat, backed by a $200 million seed from top investors, signals a shift where individual ambition could drive frontier AI forward.

2109762858703630553.name: AI Coding Benchmarks Shift with Harness Choices and Real-World Tests
2109762858703630553.summary: Tests by 8090 Labs on 113 real coding tasks showed dramatic swings: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 jumped from 41% to 61% success depending on the harness used, while no model topped its own maker's setup. Consistent performers like GPT-5.6 Sol varied by just 6 points across harnesses. The new FrontierCode 1.1 benchmark tests if AI-generated code would merge into 36 open-source repos, where top models like Claude Opus 5.5 hit only 52%—with nine tasks unsolved by any. These findings stress evaluating full model-harness combos on real workloads over synthetic leaderboards.

2112984434341204047.name: FrontierMemory Benchmark Tests AI Agents' Real Learning from Experience
2112984434341204047.summary: Letta launched FrontierMemory on October 21 to evaluate how well AI agents create useful memories from past tasks, improving performance on related coding and knowledge work without starting over. Unlike old benchmarks focused on isolated facts, it uses transcripts of prior attempts—up to six hours of memory generation—and measures gains in solve rates or cost savings on follow-ups. Top models like Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3 scored 73.3 percent, while Letta Dream led harnesses at the same mark; experts like UC Berkeley's Ion Stoica praise it for showing memory's real impact on agent growth.

2112134338275864952.name: Google Open-Sources Harness² for Self-Improving AI Agents
2112134338275864952.summary: Harness² is an open-source framework that lets AI agents refine their prompts, tools, memory, skills, and workflows recursively on each task, using evidence from test runs without needing a grader or touching the underlying model. It works through task-level loops that propose changes, probe them, and compose winners, while saving proven improvements for future jobs. Benchmarks show solid gains, like 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench for models such as GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash, and developers are already integrating it for better performance on vision tasks and more.

2109521191232794695.name: AI Paper Shows Models Learning to Revise Own Harness Code
2109521191232794695.summary: The paper 'Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation' describes a method where one AI model revises the 'harness'—the outer software layer managing tools, memory, and workflows—for another based on real results. A 4B-parameter proposer model boosted performance from 32% to 62% across 21 unseen reasoning tasks, even outperforming its larger 35B teacher, with gains persisting over repeated rounds. Elon Musk compared it to Tesla FSD absorbing hand-written C++ logic, while discussions note harnesses may evolve dynamically without vanishing entirely.

2109733556993892437.name: Fork-and-Flush Technique Boosts AI Research Agents
2109733556993892437.summary: The fork-and-flush method works by periodically copying an agent's workspace and files into multiple versions, each with a fresh chat context. The best branch continues after a short run, while others are dropped, preserving progress while sparking new directions. In tests across 13 long research tasks, it improved performance by 66% over single runs and succeeded on 12 tasks. Community members praised its lightweight design and parallels to evolutionary strategies, noting how forgetting repetitive context can unlock better results.

2109786602960453802.name: DeepRSI Benchmark Tests AI Agents on 48-Hour ML Research Tasks
2109786602960453802.summary: Jun Park, CEO of Hillclimb, launched DeepRSI to push AI agents beyond short tests, giving them 48 hours on 15 open-ended optimization problems drawn from the company's proprietary frontier research, like optimizing chess language models or speeding up GPU kernels. Agents run without internet access, with public and private verifiers preventing cheating, and an auto-resume feature prods those that quit early to continue. Claude Fable 5.1 tops the initial leaderboard at 1548 Elo, praised by observers like Audrey from Quo Labs for advancing real recursive self-improvement insights, though some question how much reflects true innovation versus known techniques. Hillclimb plans longer horizons next in this series of evals.

2112637280951378045.name: New Benchmark Tests AI's Ability to Predict Human Choices
2112637280951378045.summary: Rehearsals, Google DeepMind, and Kaggle launched Human Behavior Bench today, using surveys from 1,244 U.S. adults to test AI predictions across 750 everyday scenarios in health, finance, and more. Rehearsals’ Engram 1.0 tops the leaderboard at 94.1, outpacing models like Gemini 4 Argon (80.6) and GPT-5.6 Sol (79.5), which often default to average responses and falter on subgroups—like overestimating dislike for logo-heavy clothes. The open Kaggle dataset highlights human variation, helping build better AI simulations of real behavior.

2110693531899871616.name: Google Opens Deep Review Tool to All for Free Technical Document Checks
2110693531899871616.summary: The free tool offers two reviews per week of papers, specs, and proposals, spotting inconsistencies, missing evidence, and weak math through a multi-agent pipeline that breaks documents into sections and cross-checks them. Born from a pilot that scanned over 16,000 manuscripts at top AI conferences, it tackles the validation crunch as AI boosts content creation but human reviewers lag. Early testers praised catches like contradictions that single prompts miss, with Google stressing privacy by not training on uploads and deleting them after a year.

2112669169216790929.name: Eagle Corp Releases EAGLE-4 for 4x Faster AI Inference
2112669169216790929.summary: Eagle Corp launched EAGLE-4, an open-source system using adaptive speculative decoding where a small drafter model proposes token trees for the main model to verify quickly. Benchmarks on Qwen3.8-27B show it hitting 961.6 tokens per second on four NVIDIA B300 GPUs—about 4x faster than standard decoding—and strong results under heavy loads. Features like EAGLE-Harness optimize for hardware and workloads, with AMD support on MI355X GPUs and integrations by partners like Hyperbolic, all available on GitHub.

2111574618020725231.name: GraphRAG Outperforms Vector RAG in New UK Benchmark
2111574618020725231.summary: The UK's National Innovation Centre for Data tested 510 complex questions, where GraphRAG scored 63% truthfulness versus 35% for vector-only RAG, with better precision, recall, and answer rates. GraphRAG extracts entities and relationships into knowledge graphs for stronger multi-hop reasoning and summarization across documents. Engineers note hybrid systems combining vector efficiency for simple tasks with GraphRAG for relational questions, urging teams to test on their own data amid evolving context engineering.

2112946159161631153.name: AI Data Centers Demand $10 Trillion Investment Through 2032
2112946159161631153.summary: A Columbia Business School paper estimates $10.3 trillion in AI data center spending from 2025 to 2032, averaging 3.63% of U.S. GDP each year and surpassing past infrastructure booms like railroads at 2.2% or highways at 1.1%. To break even, AI must generate $3.5 trillion annually by 2032, or 8.8% of projected GDP, assuming high utilization and $5 per GPU-hour revenue. Skeptics highlight energy shortages and bubble risks if productivity lags, while financing shifts to leases and ventures obscure true exposure. The buildout promises capabilities but risks idle assets if growth falls short.

2112575527206969617.name: Google's Gemini 4 Argon Processes 25 Trillion Tokens in First 72 Hours
2112575527206969617.summary: Launched globally in mid-October 2026 via Gemini API, AI Studio, the app for paid users, and Google Antigravity, Argon excels in coding, finance, legal, science, and cybersecurity with its 1-million-token context window. It leads benchmarks like Isoquant's 4.38x speedup, Ramp's Accounting Bench at 61.1%, and Google's Vals Index, though T3 Code users hit 36.5 trillion tokens in the same period. Gemini 4 Carbon is already in early testing, showing gains in 3D tasks but running slower, as user feedback mixes praise for creativity with reports of crashes and quotas.
